author: Chris Compendio
description:
Both of Nintendo's Switch consoles have been cursed with deafening silence in their menus and eShops. But the latest version 23.0.0 update for the Switch 2 at least injects a little bit of personality and nostalgia into one of the platform's menus, bringing back music for the Mii Maker.

When you create a Mii in the Switch 2's system settings, the familiar Mii Channel music from the Wii now plays in the background. A music settings button on the top left also lets you change the track to the 3DS or Wii U Mii Maker music (the tracks are generically named "Track 1," Track 2," and "Track 3").

Certain Nintendo fans feel that the company's platforms have lost some of their soul with the lack of music and visual themes, so this update, as small as it is, can be taken as a nice gesture.
title: Nintendo Finally Adds Some Life To The Switch 2

author: Cheri Faulkner
description:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is overhauling the Wanted and police response systems in an interesting way. If you've played Grand Theft Auto games before, you'll know that if you do something illegal, the police will show up. You'll get a wanted level represented by stars--the more stars you have, the more aggressive the police, or even the military, will be.

In order to get out of the situation, you evade the police. You'll see them on the map, so it's easy to lay low for a minute and get them off your back. That is not the case in GTA 6. In the extended gameplay trailer, we did get a look at how some of this works, but more details have surfaced through some exclusive coverage.

The first thing we noticed was the return of the six-star wanted level. This was missing in GTA 5, but in older games if you got six stars it would cal
title: Here’s How Wanted Levels And Crime Work In GTA 6

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Marvel's Wolverine reviews have officially gone live, and while the overall consensus isn't terrible, it's not another critical hit for Spider-Man studio Insomniac Games. On GameSpot's sister site Metacritic, Marvel's Wolverine currently has a metascore of 77 from 102 reviews, with many reviewers pointing out that it doesn't live up to the standard of superhero games that Insomniac has defined with its Spider-Man adventures.

"At best, it’s a fun but forgettable experience that’ll entertain you for a few hours. At worst, it shows that just because you can make really good superhero games with one character, that doesn’t mean you can make really good super hero games with any character," editor-at-large Tamoor Hussain wrote in GameSpot's Marvel's Wolv
title: Marvel’s Wolverine Isn’t Cutting It? Try These Games Instead

title: Wardogs Has A Massive Start On Steam, But Players Face Brutal Server Queues

author: Alessandro Barbosa
description:
More than a year after its launch, the Nintendo Switch 2 finally has support for variable refresh rate when docked and connected to a TV--feature which has always been possible in portable mode.

Headlining the Switch 2 version 23.0.0 update, which is out now, VRR can now be enabled in the console's settings menu for docked play. It will require a separate update for the dock itself too, which will be applied the next time you dock the console. Also included in the update is a system-transfer feature, which might come in handy a few weeks ahead of the release of the special edition Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Nintend
title: Nintendo Adds VRR To Docked Nintendo Switch 2 Play In The Most Annoying Way

author: Tomas Franzese
description:
As part of its September update, Amazon Luna introduced a Remote Play feature that lets people play games together, even if they aren't in the same room.

If you haven't heard of it, Luna is Amazon's cloud gaming service for Prime subscribers that lets them access and play a catalog of games without the need for a console or PC. While some Luna games have had multiplayer features, you previously needed to be in the same room with others to play those titles.

Remote Play intends to solve that by letting Amazon Prime and Luna Premium subscribers invite up to seven others into their sessions. These other players won't n
title: Amazon Luna Introduces Its Most Ambitious Feature Yet In A Rough Month For Cloud Gaming

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description: The next wave of monthly games for Amazon Luna has been revealed, and if you're a fan of first-person shooters, then you're in for a treat. The headline act is Doom Eternal, or if you'd prefer your guns to be chatterboxes, you can also grab the delightfully weird High on Life. Luna members can also stream Star Wars Outlaws later this month for open-world action set in a galaxy far (far!) away, or they can explore the alien world of Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora right now.
title: Amazon Prime Members Get Doom Eternal And 10 More Games For Free In September

author: Tamoor Hussain
description:
A few hours into Wolverine I found myself asking, “Why did Insomniac Games make this?” There are obvious answers, of course: It has three excellent Spider-Man games under its belt; it's an opportunity to expand its Marvel Universe; and Wolverine presents ample opportunities for a brutal and bloody action game. But none of that explains why Insomniac Games, specifically, made Wolverine.

Spider-Man is an ideal fit for the studio: an energetic and dynamic hero in the hands of a team known for open-worlds that are sprawling jungle gyms, where it can let players loose with thrilling traversal mechanics and varied combat systems for crime fighting fun. Insomniac also excels at crafting narratives that are as earnest as they are dramatic--perfect for the tumultuous lives of Peter Parker and Miles Morales.

Wolverine is much less ideal of a pairing, as was evident
title: Wolverine Only Aims As High As Its Stout Hero

author: Tom Caswell
description: Insomniac Games takes a very safe step into the world of X-Men. Gameplay captured on PlayStation 5 Pro exclusively in the performance pro graphics mode.
title: Wolverine Only Aims As High As Its Stout Hero – Review

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
GTA 6 is one of the most-anticipated games ever, and it arrives on November 19. People naturally want to know when exactly that day it will be available to play, and now it looks the like first indication of that has come to light.

GTA Vice scoured PlayStation Store listings for the game across 63 countries and regions, and discovered that the game will not have a global simultaneous release. It looks like the US will be among the last major markets to get it.
title: Unofficial GTA 6 Worldwide Release Times Revealed, And The US Gets It Almost Last

description:
Nintendo of America has announced a "Customer Appreciation Sale," offering 30% off games and access, with Nintendo specifically citing its tariff refunds as the reason why it's running the sale, at least in part.

"The Customer Appreciation Sale is our way of saying thank you to Nintendo players for their continued support and is made possible in part by tariff-related refunds. While Nintendo absorbed most tariff-related costs, the refunds helped make promotions like this one possible," the company said.

title: Nintendo’s Latest Sale Is Made Possible By Tariff Refunds It’s Not Giving You

author: Gabe Gurwin
description:
Star Wars Zero Company released late last month, and it became one of my favorite games of the year almost instantly. I recently finished it, and while I was very satisfied with how it all wrapped up, there was one thing--a certain achievement--that was missing, and it filled me with a rage I can only satiate by complaining about it online.

You see, like the XCOM series it took so much inspiration from, Star Wars Zero Company features a permadeath mechanic. With the exception of main protagonist Hawks, any of the allies you take into battle will permanently disappear if they're killed in battle.

Aside from accidentally knocking someone off the side of the map because I was still going through the tutorial segments in the first hour or so (I restarted the mission in this case),
title: Star Wars Zero Company Is Missing The Only Achievement I Wanted

description:
I’m a huge fan of samurai games. The swift action of a fast, brutal blade, combined with beautiful takes on Japan to explore, makes them some of my favorites in my collection. I even have a Ghost of Tsushima tattoo, as Jin’s story left such a mark on me. With its sequel, Ghost of Yotei, seemingly skipping PC players, now’s your chance to give one of my other recommendations a try, especially with Rise of the Ronin at a massive 55% discount right now, making it cheaper than ever.

You’re left as a masterless samurai wandering through a Japan split between pro- and anti-shogunate factions. title: With Ghost Of Yotei Missing From PC, Rise Of The Ronin Is Worth Playing Instead At 55% Off Right Now

description:
I still vividly remember the first time I played Final Fantasy VII Remake's demo in 2019, and fully how it sold me on Square Enix's reimagining of one of the most beloved RPGs of all time. Following ex-SOLDIER Cloud's mission with Avalanche members to destroy Mako Reactor 1, the demo was perfectly paced for showcasing its beautiful modern visuals and more action-focused combat system, both of which made for an electrifying experience filled with cinematic spectacles. Fast-forward to 2026, and I'm finally playing Final Fantasy VII Revelation, the third and final part of this remake series, and it's just as surreal as it is entirely overwhelming.

title: Final Fantasy VII Revelation Hands-On Preview

author: Hayley Williams
description:
Sony has revealed today that it will no longer be working with Kojima Productions on stealth action game Physint, while Kojima announced that Xbox has stepped up to rescue the project. The change in publishers means both of Kojima's upcoming projects are now being made in partnership with Xbox, a departure from his long history of developing games for the PlayStation.

PlayStation's official statement didn't say why it chose to end its support of Physint, leaving gamers to speculate on the reasons behind its shock exit. "We continue to have great admiration for Hideo Kojima's vision for the game," Sony said, adding, "we look forward to continued close collaboration with Hideo Kojima and his award-winning independent studio in the future."
title: Kojima’s Physint Dropped By PlayStation, Rescued By Xbox

author: Blair Marnell
description:
For more than three decades, Pokemon and its various card and video games have enjoyed sustained popularity around the world.
